intro: Drafting legal memos on your Mac is a high-stakes task that demands precision and speed. If you feel overwhelmed by the process, you are not alone, as many paralegals struggle to balance accuracy with strict deadlines.

blocks.text: Why drafting legal memos is difficult

Drafting legal memos is not just about typing text. It is a complex synthesis of case law, statutes, and facts. When you write a memo, you must ensure that every citation is perfect. A single error can undermine your credibility or lead to costly revisions. The pressure to be 100% accurate while working under tight timelines is a major driver of workplace stress.

Information overload is another common issue. You often have to sift through hundreds of pages of digital evidence. Verifying every citation against primary sources like Westlaw or LexisNexis creates a rabbit hole that consumes hours. Many paralegals lose significant time just navigating between these research platforms and their drafting software.

The costs of traditional drafting workflows are high. You spend hours on administrative tasks that do not move the case forward. This includes formatting, document comparison, and manual data entry. When you add up the time spent on these non-specialized tasks, many paralegals lose four or more billable hours every week.

Burnout is the most personal cost. Nearly 30% of paralegals report feeling burned out often. This happens when the volume of work exceeds your capacity to manage it effectively. High-stakes environments require a level of focus that is hard to maintain for 40 hours a week without the right tools.

You do not need to buy expensive software to see immediate improvements. Start by building a library of templates for common memo structures. This eliminates the blank page problem and ensures consistency across your work. Use Microsoft Word features like Review > Track Changes and Compare Documents to manage your redlines efficiently.

Another fix is to change how you approach evidence review. Instead of reading every document in a linear fashion, try to extract key facts first. Use a structured summary sheet in Excel to track dates, parties, and relevant statutes. This prepares you to write the memo before you even open your drafting application.
Always check your firm's internal policy before using any AI tool. Uploading sensitive client data to third-party services can violate confidentiality rules and local regulations.

blocks.text: Lazur acts as a voice-powered assistant on your Mac. It helps you manage your workspace so you can focus on the writing itself. You can ask Lazur to walk you through complex Word settings or dictate your thoughts directly into your document.

When you are stuck, hold the shortcut to ask Lazur a question about what is on your screen. If you cannot find a specific menu item, ask Lazur where it is. It will circle the button for you. This saves you from hunting through menus when you are already in the middle of a complex drafting task.

faq.question: How can I reduce the time I spend on legal research?
faq.answer: Focus on structured data extraction. Use a spreadsheet to organize key facts before you start writing. This prevents you from jumping back and forth between research sites and your document.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI for legal writing?
faq.answer: It depends on your firm's policy. Never upload confidential client information to public AI tools. Always verify every claim and citation manually, as AI can generate errors.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle redlines in Word?
faq.answer: Use the built-in Review > Compare feature. This creates a clean document showing exactly what changed between two versions. It is much more reliable than manual tracking.
